title: The essence of calculus
beats: Series promise: 10 daily videos, calculus as binge-watchable essence
Calculus is taught as memorized rules; goal is you feel you could have invented it, as an early mathematician
Start with just you and a circle: why is area pi r squared?
Slice circle into concentric rings because it respects symmetry; pick one ring
Straighten ring to a thin rectangle: 2 pi r by dr; admit it is slightly wrong, improves as dr shrinks
dr named only after the thickness idea exists, with example value 0.1
Stand all rectangles upright side by side; heights trace graph of 2 pi r
Sum becomes a triangle area, giving pi R squared; 'beautiful argument'
Meditate on why approximate-to-exact worked: dr is both factor and spacing; smaller dr, better
Car distance from velocity times dt is the same area-under-graph shape
Pose harder graph x squared; define mystery area function A(x) (integral)
Hard problem: play instead of attack; nudge x by dx, sliver da is rectangle x^2 dx
da/dx approx x^2 is the derivative; shown at 3 and 3.001 numerically
Derivative of area gives back the graph: fundamental theorem; integrals and derivatives inverse
Peek only; details follow; reiterate you could have invented it

new_moves.name: pause-and-meditate-on-the-move
new_moves.what: After the answer, stop and name the transferable technique (approximate, sum, refine) instead of moving on
new_moves.evidence: 6:50 take a moment to meditate on why it worked

new_moves.name: play-when-stuck
new_moves.what: Explicitly tell learner to not attack hard problems directly but explore relations

new_moves.name: defer-rigor-with-permission
new_moves.what: Say it is fine to not fully get it now; later videos return

theory: The video teaches by making one familiar object (circle) carry three big ideas, and by naming the problem-solving move (approximate, then refine) separately from the answer. Each notation arrives after the picture needs it. Permission to be unclear plus a promise of invention keeps load low.
velocity: Scene builder: one concrete object (radius 3) carries the whole lesson; reuse geometry across stages (ring, rectangles, graph).
Voice: insert a explicit 'why did that work' recap beat after each payoff.
Orchestrator: allow a 'don't worry if not clear' deferral flag tied to a later-lesson pointer.
Ghost hands: nudge dx on the area slider before the ratio da/dx is named.
Evals: check that every symbol is introduced after the visual that needs it.
quote: feel that you could have invented calculus yourself
